title: Effect of Sintering Temperature on the Microstructure and Integrated Properties of MgAlTiVFeCo Lightweight High-Entropy Alloy

recollection.starting_material: Equiatomic elemental powders of Mg, Al, Ti, V, Fe, and Co
recollection.intervention: Spark plasma sintering at varied temperatures (850 °C, 900 °C, 950 °C, 1000 °C, and 1050 °C) under 50 MPa for 10 min
recollection.structure: A predominantly body‐centered cubic (BCC) solid solution with dispersed intermetallic precipitates (Laves and σ phases) whose grain size and phase fraction evolved with sintering temperature
recollection.mechanism: Higher sintering temperatures enhanced densification and atomic diffusion, promoting grain growth and precipitation of secondary phases; at moderate temperatures (950 °C–1000 °C) a balance between densification and limited grain coarsening yielded optimal microstructure
recollection.results: At 1000 °C sintering density reached ~98% of theoretical, Vickers hardness peaked at ~350 HV, compressive yield strength ~780 MPa with ~12% plastic strain; above 1000 °C, strength dropped due to excessive grain growth and phase coarsening

score.note: Correctly identifies SPS and the key 1000 °C condition, though the broader temperature schedule is not supported by the provided actual result. The recalled Laves/σ precipitates conflict with the reported oxide barrier phases and dense microstructure. The diffusion/densification explanation is only partially aligned and misses passive-film formation, chloride blocking, and parabolic oxidation kinetics. Density is reasonably close (98% vs 96.7%), but hardness is far off (350 vs 1235.5 HV), while the strength and ductility values are unsupported and corrosion/oxidation metrics are omitted.
